targets.authors: Brennan, Michael, Afroz, Sadia, and Greenstadt, Rachel
targets.title: Adversarial stylometry: Circumventing authorship recognition to preserve privacy and anonymity
targets.evidence_quote: In this paper, we report on a reproduction and, separately, a replication of the experiment described in Brennan et al. (2012).
targets.outcome_quote: The replication study generally confirms the effectiveness of the circumvention techniques reported in the original paper.
targets.outcome_computational_quote: The chosen polynomial SVM has an average accuracy of 82.1% in attributing authorship given 40 candidates (the largest candidate-pool size in our settings; 10-fold cross-validation)—virtually identical to the accuracy reported in the original study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Mixed-method paper: classified as replication because it includes a new participant sample, with one entry for its single original paper. The results explicitly provide an overall confirmation verdict; reversal of the ordering of the two methods and reduced estimated effectiveness do not override it. Reproduction axes also retained: one baseline is virtually identical, but the narrative does not establish numerical recovery across the entire central reproduction. Added feature/model specifications are described, but no self-contained verdict establishes robustness of the original-data conclusion across those alternatives.

reasoning: Published full text and references verified by exact title, DOI and three authors. Both original-data reproduction and separate new-data replication target Brennan et al. (2012). Other references supply methods or background rather than further retested published findings. Original DOI not printed in references. Uncertainty on reproduction axes is distinct from confidence in the explicit replication verdict.
